title: Review: full project code review
notes:
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM — Two P1 security/DoS vectors (NUL in message-id, uncapped newsgroups) are in validation code that was presumably carefully reviewed. The articles-table GC hole is a real storage leak under failure conditions. The stale comment is a maintenance trap. P2 issues (wildmat, race) are bounded by current deployment scale but will hurt under adversarial clients. SMTP/sieve/mail crates appear clean — no P0/P1 bugs found after comprehensive read.

Maintainer risk revised: MEDIUM-HIGH — Found 2 additional P1 bugs after deeper read: (1) blacklist system fully implemented but never integrated into accept path — blacklisted peers can still inject articles; (2) PeerRateLimiter dead code — per-connection limit only, parallel connections bypass global per-IP intent. Both are fully tested infrastructure that was built but not wired up. This is a category of bug that's hard to catch in review — the tests pass because the modules are correct in isolation.

Final confidence after reading ALL files: ~5% chance of missed bug. Coverage: read transit/main.rs accept_loop, transit/peering/peer_registry.rs (PeerRegistry instantiated only in cli/peers.rs display path, record_accepted/record_rejected never called from session), transit/gossip/swarm.rs (no bugs, best-effort channel acceptable). e4j.11 extended: not only is is_blacklisted never called, consecutive_failures also stays 0 because record_rejected is never called from session — blacklist would never auto-trigger even if check were wired in.
